questions.q: A patient with primary adrenal insufficiency has hypotension, hyponatraemia and hyperkalaemia. Which hormonal deficiency is chiefly responsible for the electrolyte abnormalities?
questions.explain: Aldosterone promotes sodium reabsorption and potassium secretion in the distal nephron. Deficiency causes renal sodium loss, reduced extracellular fluid volume and impaired potassium excretion, producing hyponatraemia and hyperkalaemia.

questions.q: Which mechanism best explains the rapid release of catecholamines from the adrenal medulla during acute stress?
options: Preganglionic sympathetic fibres release acetylcholine onto nicotinic receptors on chromaffin cells
A rise in plasma potassium directly triggers aldosterone release
questions.explain: Adrenal medullary chromaffin cells are modified postganglionic sympathetic cells. Preganglionic sympathetic fibres release acetylcholine, which activates nicotinic receptors and triggers catecholamine secretion into the bloodstream.

questions.q: Which pattern is expected after prolonged administration of exogenous glucocorticoids?
options: Suppression of hypothalamic CRH and pituitary ACTH
Selective stimulation of aldosterone with no feedback
Increased adrenal androgen synthesis from ACTH stimulation
questions.explain: Exogenous glucocorticoids exert negative feedback on hypothalamic CRH and pituitary ACTH. Prolonged suppression can cause adrenal cortical atrophy.

questions.q: In a healthy person, which factor is the principal direct regulator of aldosterone secretion during reduced effective circulating volume?
questions.explain: Reduced renal perfusion promotes renin release and angiotensin II formation. Angiotensin II directly stimulates zona glomerulosa cells; increased plasma potassium is another major stimulus.

questions.q: Which adrenal cortical zone is primarily responsible for secretion of cortisol?
questions.explain: The zona fasciculata is the principal source of glucocorticoids, especially cortisol. The zona glomerulosa produces mineralocorticoids and the zona reticularis adrenal androgens.
